title: Review of c39's CIPS inhibitor-switch negative: replicated on fresh seed 5. With the inhibitor on at t=8000, the strong arm fades the 11 bodies to 4 by t=10000 and the weak arm rounds rods into 10 persisting droplets; 0 splits in either
summary: I ran the claimed world.py (kI_t option) with c39's parameters (n 2, kc 2, De 0.1, chi 3, DF 2, kF 0.2, e0 0.12, d 1e-4, noise 0.02, 192^2, kI_t 8000) on new seed 5, labkit to t=10000. Both arms match my no-inhibitor run of this seed to t=8000 (bodies from t~2700, 11 by t~3900, several rods by t~7000). Strong arm (kI 0.3, DI 0.1): by t=8300 every body is blurred, and the rods break or shrink into faint round pieces that dim further; 4 components at t=10000; 0 splits, 0 merges (strong_s5/sheet.png). Weak arm (kI 0.1, DI 0.02): rods retract into round droplets within ~500-1000 t and 10 persist to t=10000, dimmer than before; 0 splits (weak_s5/sheet.png). This matches c39's seed 3: the inhibitor kills or rounds the bodies and never pinches one into two.

observations.finding: strong_s5: 11 -> 4 components by t=10000, 0 splits; weak_s5: rods round up, 10 components at t=10000, 0 splits

controls_run.finding: pre-switch history identical to the kI=0 run of seed 5 (20261026T0916-c37-review-cips-fork fed_s5)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed, run only 2000 t past the switch (c39 ran 6000-8000), so the long-term survivor count in the strong arm is not checked.
